nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a separable inner product space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. If $(v_i)_{i \in \iota}$ is an orthonormal family in $H$, then the index set $\iota$ is countable.
nodes.title: An orthonormal family in a separable space is countable

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a separable Hilbert space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. Then $H$ has a Hilbert basis $(e_i)_{i \in \iota}$ (an orthonormal family whose linear span is dense in $H$) indexed by a countable set $\iota$.
nodes.title: A separable Hilbert space admits a countable Hilbert basis

nodes.summary: An infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space admits a Hilbert basis indexed by $\mathbb{N}$. Let $H$ be a separable Hilbert space over $\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ that is not finite-dimensional. Then $H$ has a Hilbert basis $(e_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ indexed by the natural numbers.
nodes.title: An infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space admits a Hilbert basis indexed by $\mathbb{N}$

nodes.summary: An infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space is isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^2$. Let $H$ be a separable Hilbert space over $\mathbb{K} = \mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ that is not finite-dimensional. Then there is a $\mathbb{K}$-linear isometric isomorphism from $H$ onto $\ell^2(\mathbb{N}, \mathbb{K})$, the space of square-summable sequences in $\mathbb{K}$.
nodes.title: An infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space is isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^2$

nodes.summary: If `H` admits a Hilbert basis indexed by a countable type, then `H` is separable. No completeness hypothesis is needed: it is the density of the span of the basis, not completeness, that is used.
nodes.title: A Hilbert space with a countable orthonormal basis is separable

can_prove.label: ready to prove

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
